author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell caught George W. Bush's eyes darting side to side right before a sweet, sheepish smile crept across his face, and decided that settled the whole thing. He said the smile made it obvious the man never actually meant to start those wars, he was just doing his best. Russell delivered the line completely straight, letting the absurdity of excusing a war over a single facial expression do all the work. Sometimes the funniest commentary is the one that never raises its voice.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell explained the first lesson he ever taught his daughters, never trust authority, always assume it's corrupt, hypocritical, and trying to exploit you. He still believes every word of it, but admitted it makes parenting a nightmare. With a seven year old and a nine year old now fully applying that philosophy at home, Russell described scenes where telling them to go to their room gets met with exactly the response you'd expect. He couldn't help but call it a job well done.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell watched a senator deliver a serious speech about the sacred tradition of settling political differences at the ballot box, while a kid behind him made faces that stole every bit of attention in the room. He joked that the kid must have some connection to him, because his expressions completely undermined the whole speech without a single word. Russell admitted he shared the exact same opinion as the kid. Sometimes the audience isn't looking where you want them to.

author: Russell Brand
description:
Russell looked at that Question Time audience and read exactly what nobody on stage wanted to admit, people can see through it now. He argued the performance stopped working, the fake concern, the manufactured outrage, the endless crisis these institutions depend on to stay relevant. He said the BBC and the wider system are collapsing under their own weight, propped up only by convincing the public they still need saving. Russell claimed the contempt on those faces wasn't for the individuals on stage but for a media machine everyone can finally see is running on empty.
